title: How to get realistic Unreal environments using Claude
author: GreenCurious9895
selftext:
Has anyone achieved good results using Claude through the official MCP on Unreal 5.8 for realistic environments? I've spent alot of time trying to get realistic grasses, plants, etc and it seems like Claude really struggles with the artistic side. What methods have worked well for you? Even buying tree assets, etc it really struggles with lighting, colors, etc.

I appreciate any help!

comments.author: very_bad_programmer
comments.body:
don't aim for realism yet. Define a style and lean into a stylized look

  
We'll get there, but we're not there yet, unless you want to burn multiple weeks' worth of usage for each asset

replies.author: deReaLizedGames
replies.body: I'm in agreement here. It's way better at making stylized designs - you can either get a mediocre realistic look or a really good stylized look. As I've said in other threads: don't try to fight against AI's limitations, lean into what it's good at.

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body: Use megascans if you have access.

replies.author: GreenCurious9895
replies.body:
do you find that Claude thinks building from scratch is the best route? For example water, it recommends not using a Fluid Flux or similar and rather building a custom water system. Which it did pretty well, but not to the level you see with FF or others.

I'm wondering if I need to switch strategies and really go the megascan/FAB/plugin route and keep Claude off the art parts.

replies.author: HaMMeReD
replies.body:
You need to take the reigns and make decisions for yourself when it comes to architecture and components.

Ultimately Claude is a tool, it'll lean certain ways but it's not universally right. I.e. I do actually have a bespoke fluid simulation right now, but I also have a custom 2D engine and that was a choice.

But when I use Unreal, I have all the Megascan assets, why fight with photo-realism when I have a bunch of appropriately licensed assets and plugins like Ultra Dynamic Sky, I use them. The Agent gets no say on it. I haven't done Unreal for about a year or so, but it's much easier to select an asset from a library and place it with MCP in the world, then it is to generate an asset from scratch.

When you see people modeling things in 3D with Claude or Codex fable or astra, that doesn't mean it's a cost-effective use of a LLM. I'd focus on things it does well, i.e. MCP interfaces and code.

replies.author: HaMMeReD
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/kv6pr0v79pth1.png?width=496&format=png&auto=webp&s=c284df81990f814650ebff060ece647cfd2bc3d7

As for assets, if you must make your own. Use an appropriate ai model. I use Meshy on my dog 3d printing service, i.e. above image. Was generated by taking dog-photos to a generative 4-up reference sheet, then split and passed to meshy to make the mesh.

The entire generation maybe costs 25-50 cents total. Although I would only use for static meshes in a game (I.e. I wouldn't rig this dog). Although I think things are getting better there.
